class_name: 強調-問題なし-トイウ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

glosses: every single … (in the frame N という N)
patterns.usage_note: Emphatic という, not the quotative or naming one: it re-presents a noun in order to hold it up for attention, so 今日という日 is "today, of all days" rather than merely "today". When the same noun is repeated on both sides (店という店, 木という木) the frame sweeps the whole category — "every last shop" — and this repeated shape is especially at home in narrative and descriptive writing. The nuance is emotional weight or exhaustiveness, so a plain 今日は or 店が is the neutral alternative whenever that weight is unwanted.

examples.ruby: 今日[きょう]という日[ひ]は、二度[にど]と戻[もど]ってこない。
examples.english: Today, this day of all days, will never come again.

examples.ruby: 祖父[そふ]という人[ひと]は、一度[いちど]も弱音[よわね]を吐[は]かなかった。
examples.english: My grandfather, the man he was, never once let out a word of complaint.

examples.ruby: 台風[たいふう]の翌朝[よくあさ]、店[みせ]という店[みせ]が閉[し]まっていた。
examples.english: The morning after the typhoon, every last shop was shuttered.
